title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: From a 26-mile campus relay to a physics-defying pumpkin drop, discover the rituals that define the Spartan experience at Case Western Reserve University.

cards.title: The 26-Mile Campus Sprint
cards.subtitle: A marathon-length relay race through campus
cards.notes: Runners from each class compete in a 26-mile relay to commemorate the university's 1882 move from Hudson to Cleveland.
cards.short_summary: An annual 26-mile relay race where undergraduate classes compete for bragging rights and a spot on the commemorative rock.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hudson Relays is an annual 26-mile relay through campus intended to commemorate Western Reserve College's move from Hudson, Ohio.
cards.source_title: Hudson Relays | Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Held annually in April; spectators can watch from various points along the campus route.

cards.title: The Ultimate Finals Break
cards.subtitle: Late-night food and games in Thwing Center
cards.notes: Take a break from finals with free food, massages, and activities held every semester before exams begin.
cards.short_summary: A massive late-night event providing students with food and stress-relief activities during the final exam period.
cards.evidence_claim: Thwing Study Over is the perfect break from studying as you prepare for finals every fall and spring semester.
cards.source_title: Thwing Study Over | Student Activities and Leadership
cards.access_notes: Occurs late at night during finals week; check the student activities calendar for specific hours.

cards.title: The 'Lipstick' Physics Tribute
cards.subtitle: A monument to the famous 'aether' experiment
cards.notes: Commonly called the 'lipstick fountain,' this sculpture's water symbolizes the ether waves disproved in 1887.
cards.short_summary: A landmark fountain on the Case Quad commemorating the 1887 experiment that disproved the existence of luminiferous aether.
cards.evidence_claim: The Michelson-Morley Fountain was constructed in 1973 to commemorate the 1886 experiment that disproved the theory of the 'aether.'
cards.source_title: Guess Where: Michelson-Morley Fountain | CWRU Newsroom
cards.access_notes: Located outdoors on the Case Quad; accessible 24/7.

cards.title: The Campus Message Board
cards.subtitle: A dedicated space for student expression
cards.notes: Student groups paint this wall near the Tinkham Veale University Center to promote events and advocacy.
cards.short_summary: A designated campus wall where student organizations can paint messages and advertisements for upcoming activities.
cards.evidence_claim: The primary purpose of the Spirit Wall is to draw attention to campus events and activities planned by student groups.
cards.source_title: Student Advocacy and Spirit Wall Policy
cards.access_notes: Visible to the public; painting is restricted to recognized student groups following university policy.

cards.title: The Physics Pumpkin Drop
cards.subtitle: Testing gravity from the roof of Strosacker Hall
cards.notes: Every Halloween, the physics department drops pumpkins frozen in liquid nitrogen to demonstrate gravity.
cards.short_summary: A Halloween tradition where physics students drop frozen pumpkins from the roof of Strosacker Hall to observe the impact.
cards.evidence_claim: Around Halloween the physics department checks gravity with the pumpkin drop off the roof of Strosacker.
cards.access_notes: Annual event held around Halloween; open for public viewing from the quad.

cards.title: The Year-End Celebration
cards.subtitle: Inflatables, food, and live music on the quad
cards.notes: Celebrate the end of the spring semester with a day of carnival games, food trucks, and a headlining concert.
cards.short_summary: A student-run festival held on the last Saturday of the spring semester featuring music and campus-wide activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Springfest, which occurs the last Saturday of the spring semester, is a student-planned event that celebrates CWRU.
cards.access_notes: Held annually in late April; open to all CWRU students.

cards.title: The Engineering Egg Drop Twist
cards.subtitle: Protecting a lightbulb from a multi-story fall
cards.notes: During Engineers Week, students design contraptions to prevent a lightbulb from breaking when dropped in the library.
cards.short_summary: A competitive event during E-Week where teams build protective housing for lightbulbs dropped from the Kelvin Smith Library balcony.
cards.evidence_claim: The WISER Lightbulb Drop allows participants to showcase engineering skills in a competition at Kelvin Smith Library.
cards.source_title: Engineers Week 2020 - Case School of Engineering
cards.access_notes: Held annually during Engineers Week in February; spectators welcome in the library atrium.

cards.title: A Mascot's Annual Bash
cards.subtitle: Celebrating the Spartan mascot
cards.notes: Join the campus community for cake and festivities to celebrate the birthday of Spartie, the CWRU mascot.
cards.short_summary: An annual campus event featuring cake and photos to celebrate the university's mascot, Spartie.
cards.evidence_claim: The Office of Student Activities & Leadership supports campus events including Spartie's Birthday Party.
cards.source_title: Campus Traditions & Events | Student Activities and Leadership
cards.access_notes: Typically held in the Tinkham Veale University Center; open to all students.

cards.title: The Gravity-Inspired Clone
cards.subtitle: A direct descendant of Isaac Newton's tree
cards.notes: Visit the tree on the Case Quad that was grafted from the original apple tree at Isaac Newton's home.
cards.short_summary: A tree on campus that is a genetic clone of the apple tree that reportedly inspired Isaac Newton's theory of gravity.
cards.evidence_claim: The Newton apple tree was grafted (i.e., cloned) from the old apple tree outside Woolsthorpe Manor.
cards.source_title: Walking tour shows campus through the accomplishments of Michelson and Morley
cards.access_notes: Located on the Case Quad near the Michelson-Morley plaque; accessible 24/7.

cards.title: The Campus Trick-or-Treat
cards.subtitle: Halloween festivities across campus offices
cards.notes: Students visit various campus departments and offices to collect candy and meet university staff.
cards.short_summary: A Halloween tradition where students 'crawl' through campus buildings to receive treats from participating offices.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Traditions & Events include the CWRU Candy Crawl.
cards.source_title: Campus Traditions & Events | Student Activities and Leadership
cards.access_notes: Held annually on or near Halloween during business hours.
